findings.what: The new sleep unit still declares func_00d904 as int despite its short definition, without an ORIGINAL BUG interface qualification. Unlike the byte-assignment callers in mole/projectiles, this caller needs no mismatch to match: changing to short preserves both full functions in both revisions. Sleep also declares MovePadInputIntoD0 as int while its accepted definition and several callers use long. Both are 32-bit in this compiler, so no byte difference is observed, but int and long are distinct C interface types.
findings.suggested_fix: Use extern short func_00d904() and extern long MovePadInputIntoD0() in sleep.c, retaining int GetActivePresentSprite(). The complete private alternatives/long-pad-sleep/sleep.c independently MATCHes both revisions. Preserve the explicitly qualified int exceptions only in callers where the original bytes actually require them. Carry existing abs int/long disagreements into the shared-interface reconciliation rather than claiming global consistency.

findings.what: The two new tile-buffer consumers declare ram_ffb8da as char[8192], while the accepted DMA consumer still declares the same named object as unsigned short[]. These are incompatible extern types, not merely different local typed pointers. The new bounded byte view is compiler-sensitive and useful, but the cross-unit mismatch is not locally reconciled. No binary discrepancy was observed.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same bounded byte declaration in load_sprites.c and convert that named storage to an unsigned-short pointer locally for DMA traversal. alternatives/consistent-buffer/load_sprites.c does exactly this and independently MATCHes both revisions. Describe the 8192-byte capacity as the inferred available span to the adjacent state word, unless an independent allocation/bounds source is established.

findings.what: The cast on the tiny direction mask, state->sprite & (unsigned long)3, is deliberately compiler-sensitive: replacing it with the plain integer mask preserves the 376-byte function extent but changes scratch registers. The author handoff records that fact, but source has no local disclosure. A conventional 3U spelling is rejected by MCC68K. This is not a prohibited address trick or a behavioral bug; the precise historical spelling remains [INFERENCE].
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short local compiler-choice qualification explaining that an unsigned 32-bit mask preserves the observed operand/register order, without claiming it was proved to be the historical source; alternatively retain a simpler independently matching spelling if one is found. No gameplay or control-flow change is requested.

If intentionally deferred, record F2 as an outstanding qualification instead of claiming it resolved.

qualification_summary: No blocking byte mismatch, prohibited source device, stale prepare input, unsubstantiated revision guard, changed moved-function body or false-positive negative control was found. All sixteen new files received a deep sample, and both normal full ROMs reproduce exactly. Acceptance is qualified by avoidable sleep/buffer interface differences, an undisclosed compiler-sensitive mask choice and the still-open C010 F2 source qualification. The mole/projectiles implicit-int explanation is experimentally plausible, correctly marked [INFERENCE], and not evidence of a uniquely recovered historical declaration. Existing shared-header/layout and older scalar-interface debt is not claimed resolved. Private alternatives were matched, not adopted or accepted as new checkpoint inputs.
